usdRate.sourceName: Central Bank of Yemen (Aden), Monetary and financial developments, May 2026
usdRate.note: Average market rate of 1,562.49 rials per US dollar in May 2026 (1,562.93 in April). Figures are for the central bank in Aden; areas run by the Sanaa authorities use older banknotes at a different exchange rate and restrict interest. Trading Economics still shows an outdated official rate of about 236.

inflation_cpi.note: No year-on-year inflation rate could be read: the Central Bank of Yemen's May 2026 report gives only the monthly CPI change (index 98.19 to 100.05, +1.89% in May 2026, from the Central Statistical Organization), the statistics office site refused requests, and the World Bank's latest figure is from 2014.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Central Bank of Yemen (Aden): monthly CPI +1.89% in May 2026; rial 1,562 per dollar after a 2025 peak near 2,900
inflation_projection.note: Inflation in government areas ran at 20 to 30% a year during the currency collapse before the 2025-2026 stabilisation, so a planning rate of 15% allows for renewed depreciation.

policy_rate.note: The Central Bank of Yemen (Aden) sets a minimum rate on rial savings deposits (18%) and a 20% coupon on one-year treasury bills, but publishes no single policy rate; Trading Economics' 27% is from 2022. Figures are for the central bank in Aden; areas run by the Sanaa authorities use older banknotes at a different exchange rate and restrict interest.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Central Bank of Yemen (Aden), Monetary and financial developments, May 2026
savings_account_rate.note: The central bank set the interest rate on new rial savings deposits at commercial banks at 18% a year and leaves term deposit rates to banks. Figures are for the central bank in Aden; areas run by the Sanaa authorities use older banknotes at a different exchange rate and restrict interest.

fdr_3m_rate.note: Banks set term deposit rates freely (Central Bank of Yemen, May 2026) and no industry-wide 3-month rate is published.

fdr_1y_rate.note: Banks set term deposit rates freely (Central Bank of Yemen, May 2026) and no industry-wide 1-year rate is published.

dps_rate.note: No monthly recurring deposit product or published rate was found.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: No current weighted average deposit rate was found; the World Bank's latest value is 15.25% for 2013, too old to use.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate sold to individuals was confirmed.

tbill_91d_rate.note: The Central Bank of Yemen (Aden) currently auctions one-year treasury bills at a 20% coupon (auction of 4 November 2026, minimum bid 50 million rials) to banks; no 3-month yield is published.

tbond_5y_rate.note: No 5-year government bond yield is published.

tbond_10y_rate.note: No 10-year government bond yield is published.

tax_bank_interest.note: The tax treatment of bank interest for individuals could not be confirmed; PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries does not cover Yemen and the Tax Authority site could not be found.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: There is no government savings certificate for individuals, and the tax on government security interest could not be confirmed.

deposit_insurance_limit.note: No deposit insurance scheme or cover amount was found for Yemeni banks.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap or typical credit card rate was found; lending rates are set freely by banks (Central Bank of Yemen, May 2026).

equity_return_low.sourceName: No stock exchange in Yemen; global equities in rial terms; rial 1,562 per dollar (May 2026)
equity_return_low.note: Low case: global equities earn little in dollars while the rial holds steady.

equity_return_base.sourceName: No stock exchange in Yemen; global equity index about 7% a year in dollars; rial depreciation assumed about 8% a year
equity_return_base.note: Yemen has no stock market, so the base case is a global index in rial terms (about 7% in dollars plus about 8% a year of depreciation), below the 18% savings rate plus 4 points.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Global equity index in rial terms; rial history (about 250 per dollar in 2014 to 1,562 in May 2026)
equity_return_high.note: High case: strong global markets and a renewed sharp rial depreciation.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Rial 1,562 per dollar (May 2026), stable since August 2025
gold_return_low.note: Low case: flat dollar gold and a stable rial.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Rial 1,562 per dollar (May 2026); inflation assumption 15%; long-run dollar gold trend about 4%
gold_return_base.note: Base case: about 4% dollar gold trend plus about 9% a year of rial depreciation.

gold_return_high.sourceName: Rial history: 1,756 per dollar in May 2024, 2,534 in May 2025, 1,562 in May 2026 (Central Bank of Yemen)
gold_return_high.note: High case: strong dollar gold and a renewed collapse of the rial like 2021-2025.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Yemen: 18% on new rial savings deposits (May 2026)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: deposit rates fall as the rial stabilises, and liquidity limits at banks reduce what savers actually earn.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Central Bank of Yemen: 18% on new rial savings deposits (May 2026); one-year treasury bills at 20%
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: well below the posted 18% savings rate because tax treatment is unconfirmed and bank liquidity and cash-withdrawal limits make the posted rate hard to earn in full.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Central Bank of Yemen: 18% on new rial savings deposits; one-year treasury bills at 20% (November 2026 auction)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: the full posted savings rate.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: No industry-wide life claim settlement ratio was found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: No published term life premium rates per YER 1,000 by age were found; the life insurance market is very small.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: No published typical cost of a major private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: No published private health insurance premiums by age were found.

oop_health_share.sourceName: World Bank WDI, out-of-pocket expenditure (% of current health expenditure), Yemen
oop_health_share.note: 69.1% in 2023 (WHO Global Health Expenditure Database via the World Bank); older than 2025, the latest available.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Inflation assumption 15%; imported medicines priced in dollars
goal_inflation_health.note: Medicines and private care are largely imported and priced off the dollar, so health goals are planned 2 points above the general assumption.

goal_inflation_education.note: No education price index could be read, so education goals use the general assumption.

life_expectancy.sourceName: World Bank WDI, life expectancy at birth, total (SP.DYN.LE00.IN), Yemen

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 medium variant for 2026; the 65 total is published there, the other totals are the mean of men and women.

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 4.51 (2025, World Bank), 5.9 (2040) and 12.2 (2065, populationpyramid.net/yemen/2065/).

retirement_age_default.note: The pension age under the Social Insurance Law for private-sector workers could not be read from an official source; the social security corporation's site could not be found and the US SSA country pages refused requests.

retirement_age_government.note: The retirement age for civil servants could not be read from an official source.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: Central Bank of Yemen: 18% on new rial savings deposits (May 2026)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: deposit rates fall and access to deposits stays limited.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Central Bank of Yemen: 18% on new rial savings deposits (May 2026)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case: below the posted savings rate, allowing for unconfirmed tax and bank liquidity limits, so not above the after-tax safe rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Central Bank of Yemen: 18% on new rial savings deposits; one-year treasury bills at 20%
retirement_return_high.note: High case: near the posted savings rate.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Fixed income low 8%; equity low 6%; gold low 4%
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case: a mix of rial deposits, gold and foreign assets earning little.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Fixed income base 12%; global equity base 15%; gold base 13%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: a balanced mix of rial deposits, gold and global equities.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case: a growth-leaning mix with rial depreciation boosting foreign assets.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: The Social Welfare Fund pays means-tested cash transfers to poor households, including elderly people, but its current amount and whether payments are regular could not be confirmed.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Social Welfare Fund cash transfers target poor households rather than an age group; no age-based eligibility rule was found.

gratuity_rule.note: The Labour Code (Law No. 5 of 1995) is reported to provide an end-of-service award for workers not covered by social insurance, but its terms could not be read from an official source.

public_pension_scheme.note: Public-sector employees are insured by the General Authority for Social Insurance and Pensions and private-sector employees by the General Corporation for Social Security, but pension ages and indexation could not be read from an official source.

savings_account.note: The central bank sets 18% a year on new rial savings deposits (May 2026).

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring deposit was confirmed.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificate for individuals was confirmed.

tbill_91d.note: The central bank auctions one-year bills to banks with a 50 million rial minimum bid; no 3-month bills for individuals.

tbond_5y.note: No retail government bonds were found.

tbond_10y.note: No retail government bonds were found.

equity_fund.note: Yemen has no stock exchange or regulated retail mutual funds.

gold.note: Gold jewellery and coins are widely bought as savings.

centralBank.name: Central Bank of Yemen (head office, Aden)
